claims.text: At high temperatures, plastic strain capacity and toughness in fusion plasma-facing structural materials are primarily governed by grain-boundary integrity.
Segregation of impurities such as oxygen and sulfur embrittles grain boundaries and controls grain-boundary sliding and cavitation.
Ultra-clean processing or impurity scavenging should reduce impurity segregation and enhance grain-boundary cohesion.
Enhanced grain-boundary cohesion should increase plastic strain capacity and toughness.
Standard powder metallurgy followed by hot isostatic pressing can produce a homogeneous fusion-relevant alloy microstructure with conventional impurity levels.
The controlled comparison should use ultra-low-impurity and standard-impurity samples while holding grain size, precipitate content, and nominal alloy composition constant.
Mechanical testing should consist of tensile or creep tests at 800–1000°C under an inert atmosphere with controlled strain rates and holding times.
Loading at 800–1000°C under inert conditions can simulate relevant cyclic or long-duration fusion service loading.
At high temperatures, impurities tend to segregate to grain boundaries and reduce intergranular cohesion.
Reduced intergranular cohesion promotes grain-boundary sliding and cavitation.
Grain-boundary cavitation accelerates deformation localization and reduces toughness.
Reducing impurity content preserves grain-boundary strength during high-temperature deformation.
Ultra-low-impurity samples should exhibit greater plastic strain capacity and fracture toughness than standard-impurity samples.
Ultra-low-impurity samples should show less grain-boundary impurity enrichment and fewer signs of grain-boundary cavitation.
The hypothesis is expected to apply between 800°C and 1000°C under inert-atmosphere conditions.
The hypothesis may have limited applicability in oxidizing or highly reactive environments.
Changes in grain size or precipitate behavior may alter the proposed impurity-segregation effect.
The magnitude of improvement and the critical impurity concentration thresholds are unknown.

Failure of ultra-low-impurity samples to show a statistically significant increase in both plastic strain capacity and toughness, or failure of reduced segregation to correlate with improved performance, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention requires refined purification and impurity-scavenging treatments for one sample set, whereas the falsification design says the two sets will use identical processing methods. Distinct purification treatments cannot literally be identical processing unless the statement is narrowed to identical downstream processing.

The intervention says bulk composition is held constant while impurity content is deliberately changed. Because impurities are part of bulk composition, this requires clarification that only the nominal matrix-alloy composition, rather than total chemical composition, is held constant.
